text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and create human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learn from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites, and articles. To get good results, users often use prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs can help with tasks like answering questions, translating, or writing texts. However, they also have limits. They sometimes make mistakes, cannot truly understand meaning, and may repeat false information from their training data.
